answer: Each AI grader is tied to a unique computational knoll—a hardware enclave whose cryptographic fingerprint is logged at the network vertex in a basalt ledger of identity. A random jury of peers periodically spot‑checks a sample of these fingerprints, rejecting any node whose live enclave hash does not match the basalt record. Thus an attacker must purchase and maintain a full enclave for each fake identity, driving cost up linearly with the number of Sybils and deterring large‑scale attacks.
